The Louisiana Purchase treaty was signed in 1803 between the United States and France. The American negotiators were Robert Livingston and James Monroe, who were appointed by President Thomas Jefferson to handle the negotiations. François Barbé-Marbois was the French Minister of Finance and signed on behalf of France.

Thomas Jefferson, as President, authorized the purchase and played a crucial role in the decision-making process, but he did not personally sign the treaty.

Therefore, the actual signatories of the Louisiana Purchase treaty were Robert Livingston, James Monroe, and François Barbé-Marbois.
